messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: ellen.strat@strategyfirm.com
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft: Converging Serving & Infra Squads — Org note + QBR talking points

Team —

I want to get alignment before the QBR on a proposed consolidation of the Serving Runtime and Infrastructure Platform squads into a single group (working name: Serving & Platform). The goal is to reduce handoffs, simplify release ownership for runtime optimizations, and create a single product surface for customers around "serving economics" (latency/cost/reliability).

High-level proposal (summary):
- Combine 5 squads (Runtime, KV Cache, Batch & Autoscale, Infra Ops, Kernel Workloads) into 3 cross-functional squads focused on: Runtime Core, Serving Controls (autoscale, caching, routing), and Platform Ops (SRE, deploy).
- Leadership: interim alignment under the current Runtime lead for 6 weeks; identify permanent GM by mid-Q1.
- Timeline: announce internally 12/03, begin phased transfers 01/03, complete org baseline by 03/01.

Primary risks to surface at QBR:
- Short-term velocity drop for performance work (2–4 weeks).
- Customer SLAs for Dedicated capacity changes during migration window.
- Required updates to billing and console UI flows.

Attached is a working draft of the announcement, QBR talking points, and a timeline with risk mitigations. Please review and call out anything that must be addressed before I share a 12/03 internal note.

Key asks:
1) Jonas — can you review the leadership language and any customer escalation play changes?
2) Marissa — need the go-to-market readouts and any customer-facing comm ask (timing/limits).
3) Karthik & Mina — org-level concerns, spans-of-control, and capacity for hiring/backfills.

I want the final version by EOD 12/01 so we can lock the 12/03 announcement slot on all-hands.

Thanks —
Sooj

--
Soojin Lee
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Sooj — thanks for the clear framing. A few edits from my side after skimming the announcement:

1) Leadership wording: avoid implying an immediate search for a GM; phrase as \"identify and appoint a permanent head by mid-Q1, with an internal candidate preferred\". We should make clear who will cover cross-squad PM responsibilities during the interim.

2) Customer impact: the bit about \"Dedicated capacity changes\" needs a short parenthetical with mitigation (e.g., pre-allocated reservation hold for existing contracts + SLA exceptions managed via GTM).

3) QBR talking points: add a slide that quantifies expected 90-day delta in token-cost and latency for representative workloads (we can use data from the cost/perf lab). Even if rough, it helps executives and sales make decisions.

I'll add inline comments directly to the Drive doc.

—Jonas

Adding marketing and sales perspective:

- We need a short external comm plan for customers who have early access or Dedicated contracts. Proposed approach: 2-week heads-up to affected customers with an opt-in \"no-change\" window if they prefer stability until their next renewal.
- Pricing: if there's any potential near-term impact to unit economics (e.g., improved cost/latency tradeoffs), we should avoid publishing numbers in the initial announcement. Keep it directional and promise a follow-up data deck during QBR.
- Sales enablement: please include a one-page \"FAQ for AMs\" in the Drive link for use starting 12/06.

I put a few suggested edits in the draft doc and flagged a handful of accounts that need special handling (Acme Platform Team is listed).

Couple of org-level notes from People/Managers perspective:

- Spans: when you collapse five squads into three, please ensure no manager is asked to immediately increase direct reports beyond 8-10 without an explicit headcount plan. That should be in the announcement or the separate manager transition checklist.
- Hiring/backfills: we need a prioritized hiring pipeline for infra SREs; please link to req IDs. If we move the timeline earlier, we should protect runway for critical hires.
- Performance reviews: clarify how career ladder assessments will occur for impacted ICs — specifically those in kernel/low-level ops. We should avoid any perception of forced movement.

I added a manager checklist tab in the timeline spreadsheet attached.

-Karthik

2) Publish a public FAQ page for customers within 24 hours of the internal note to reduce inbound tickets.

Happy to hop on a 30-min prep call this afternoon if helpful.
